requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
I judge the {test} items for `requirements.references.outline_selectors` adequate. I did not request any implementation source. Each obligation maps to a test with assertions, as follows.

- **Path form and empty selector.**
  - `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` asserts that `parse_selector("")` is empty. It parses a multi-segment path and rejects malformed ones: `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]`, `a//b`, `fn[run]x`.
  - `tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` asserts that `resolve("")` returns the root, index 0. It also resolves nested paths such as `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`.
  - `tests.rs#fn[profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent]` asserts that an unmatched selector gives a "no outline node matches" error and a malformed one gives an `Invalid` error.
  - `tests/search.rs#fn[outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reinterpreting_resources]` accepts `""`, `fn[kept]` and `mod[a%2Fb]/fn[kept]`. It rejects `fn[missing`, `fn[bad%ZZ]` and `/fn[kept]`.

- **Named segments `kind[name]`.** `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks about 20 named selectors across kinds. Each one is present in the outline, and it resolves back to a node with the same selector.

- **Anonymous segments `kind@hash`, first 12 hex digits of the identity hash.**
  - `tests.rs#fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` checks the `use@` prefix and a 12-character hash.
  - It also checks that inserting a line before leaves the old selectors resolvable. That means line numbers are not part of the selector.
  - It checks that editing the node's own text invalidates its selector.
  - `tests.rs#fn[anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits]` asserts the selector is exactly `pair[items]/item@<identity_hash[..12]>`. The selector stays stable and resolvable after a descendant edit, while the structural hash changes. It also resolves a child path beneath the anonymous segment.
  - `markdown_tests.rs#fn[paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges]` checks the `kind@` prefix and 12-digit length for Markdown anonymous nodes, and that every selector resolves to its own node.
  - The parse test normalizes the hash to lowercase and rejects `use@123`.

- **`#N` disambiguation, one-based, in source order.**
  - `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2` resolve in `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry`.
  - The bare `fn[repeated]` is rejected there, so the ordinal is required for duplicates.
  - Duplicate anonymous `use` nodes end in `#1` and `#2` in `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes`.
  - `#0` is rejected in the parse test.
  - A unique selector such as `struct[Packet]` has no ordinal.

- **`line` exception.** `tests.rs#fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` has identical lines `alpha` at two positions. They get identical selectors with no `#N`, and the selector resolves, to the first match. It also checks that the whitespace-word rule applies to line hashes: `two  words` and `two words` give the same selector, and `twowords` gives a different one.

- **Percent-encoding.** `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding]` covers `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@`, space and tab. It also covers non-ASCII and Unicode whitespace (nbsp, ideographic space), encoded as UTF-8 bytes. It checks the exact encoded string and the decode round trip. It also asserts that raw `/`, malformed `%zz` and raw space are rejected on decode. The real-outline case `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` shows encoding in an actual selector.

- **No line numbers in selectors.** This is shown indirectly by the shifted-line resolution in `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes`, and by the line selectors being content-derived.

The structural-hash computation itself belongs to `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which this requirement cites. I did not reassess it. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
